g.text: Two public clues break the herd (working title)
100 people chose blue. How much do they know?
Clues are right 2 times in 3. From person 3 on, a lead of 2 outweighs any clue.
Two chose blue, then 98 followed. Now two new private clues
are published: both red. Your own clue is red. Choose?
Two public clues break the herd (working title)
100 people chose blue. How much do they know?
Clues are right 2 times in 3. From person 3 on, a lead of 2 outweighs any clue.
1-2: chose on a blue clue. 3-100: followed.
Hint: count the clues behind the crowd, then publish the two clues.
Two public clues break the herd (working title)
100 people chose blue. How much do they know?
Clues are right 2 times in 3. From person 3 on, a lead of 2 outweighs any clue.
1-2: chose on a blue clue. 3-100: followed.
The 98 followers ignored their clues, so 100 blue choices
held 2 blue clues. With yours alone, blue stayed 67%.
Two published reds plus yours make 3 red to 2 blue:
blue falls to 33%. Red is the better choice; the herd can flip.
